반갑다.m: glad (to see/meet), pleased, nice to meet
반갑다.t: Formal greeting: 만나서 반갑습니다. Use it for meeting someone, not for being happy in general (that's 기쁘다).

비행기표.x: I bought a plane ticket to go home over vacation.

만족하다.m: to be satisfied, to be content
만족하다.x: I'm very satisfied with my life right now.
만족하다.t: Pronounced [만조카다]; 'satisfied with something' is N에 만족하다.

남성.ex: 이 옷은 남성과 여성 모두 입을 수 있습니다.
남성.x: These clothes can be worn by both men and women.
남성.t: 남성 is formal, seen in news, signs and surveys; in conversation say 남자.

참석하다.m: to attend, to be present at
참석하다.x: Please be sure to attend tomorrow's meeting.
참석하다.e: Literally 'join a seat' — take your place at the event.
참석하다.t: Use N에 참석하다 for meetings, weddings and ceremonies: 결혼식에 참석했어요.

질병.ex: 손을 자주 씻으면 많은 질병을 예방할 수 있어요.
질병.x: Washing your hands often can prevent many diseases.
질병.t: 질병 is formal and written; in conversation people usually just say 병.

구청.x: After moving, I went to the district office and reported it.
구청.e: Literally 'district office'; big cities like Seoul are divided into 구, such as 강남구.

옳다.x: What the teacher said is right.
옳다.t: Pronounced [올타]; in 옳아요 [오라요] the ㅎ goes silent.

과학 기술.x: Thanks to advances in science and technology, life has become convenient.

진행되다.m: to proceed, to be in progress, to be held
진행되다.ex: 오늘 행사는 비가 와도 예정대로 진행됩니다.
진행되다.x: Today's event will go ahead as planned even if it rains.
진행되다.e: Literally 'advance and go', plus 되다: the thing goes ahead.

하락하다.m: to fall, to drop, to decline
하락하다.x: Gas prices have been dropping little by little since yesterday.
하락하다.t: Pronounced [하라카다]; in conversation people usually say 떨어지다 instead.

계층.ex: 사회의 모든 계층이 이 정책의 영향을 받습니다.
계층.x: Every class of society is affected by this policy.
계층.t: 계층 is about income or social layers; 계급 suggests rigid ranks, like in the military or a caste system.

한약.x: Herbal medicine tastes bitter, so it's hard to take.

수립하다.m: to establish, to set up (a plan, policy, government)
수립하다.x: The government established a new economic policy.
수립하다.e: Literally 'plant and make stand' — setting up a plan firmly.
수립하다.t: Collocates with 계획, 정책, 대책, 전략; everyday equivalent is 계획을 세우다.

유력하다.ex: 그 후보가 이번 선거에서 가장 유력합니다.
유력하다.x: That candidate is the most likely to win this election.
유력하다.t: Pronounced [유려카다]; common in news: 유력한 후보 (frontrunner), 유력 인사 (influential figure).

불현듯.m: suddenly (of a thought or feeling), out of the blue
불현듯.ex: 길을 걷다가 불현듯 옛 친구가 보고 싶어졌어요.
불현듯.x: While walking down the street, I suddenly missed an old friend.
불현듯.e: Probably from 불 'fire' plus an old verb 'to light' — a thought flaring up.

빼곡히.ex: 공책에 작은 글씨가 빼곡히 적혀 있어요.
빼곡히.x: The notebook is crammed with tiny handwriting.
빼곡히.e: Adverb of 빼곡하다; close in meaning to 빽빽이 'densely'.

무용지물.m: useless thing, something of no use
무용지물.x: Once the battery dies, even a smartphone is useless.

주객전도.m: role reversal; the side issue overshadowing the main thing
주객전도.x: If the wrapping costs more than the gift, you've got it backward.
주객전도.e: Literally 'host and guest turned upside down.'
rel: putting the cart before the horse

장학생.x: He was selected as a scholarship student because of his good grades.

뒷말.m: gossip, talk behind one's back; the rest of what was said
뒷말.ex: 회의가 끝나고 사람들 사이에서 뒷말이 많았어요.
뒷말.x: After the meeting, there was a lot of talk behind people's backs.
뒷말.e: 뒤 'behind, after' + 말 'words': words said behind, or afterward.
뒷말.t: Pronounced [뒨말] — nasalization; 뒷말이 나오다 means 'people start talking (critically).'

돌풍.m: sensation, upset, stir; sudden gust of wind
돌풍.ex: 신인 가수가 데뷔하자마자 음원 차트에서 돌풍을 일으켰어요.
돌풍.x: The new singer caused a sensation on the music charts right after debuting.
돌풍.t: Common pattern: 돌풍을 일으키다, often about a newcomer or underdog's surprising success.

변명하다.m: to make excuses, justify oneself, explain oneself
변명하다.ex: 늦은 이유를 변명하지 말고 먼저 사과하세요.
변명하다.x: Don't make excuses for being late; apologize first.
변명하다.e: Literally 'to distinguish and make clear' one's case.
변명하다.t: 변명 sounds defensive; for a neutral official explanation, use 해명하다.

설욕.ex: 작년 결승에서 진 팀이 올해 설욕에 성공했어요.
설욕.x: The team that lost last year's final got its revenge this year.
설욕.e: Literally 'wash away disgrace' — the first syllable is 'snow', used here as 'cleanse'.
설욕.t: Used for sports and competitions; 설욕전 is a rematch where the loser seeks revenge.

팔은 안으로 굽는다.forms: 팔은 안으로 굽는다고 · 팔이 안으로 굽다
팔은 안으로 굽는다.m: people naturally side with their own; blood is thicker than water (lit. arms bend inward)
팔은 안으로 굽는다.ex: 팔은 안으로 굽는다고, 엄마는 늘 제 편만 들어요.
팔은 안으로 굽는다.x: Blood is thicker than water: Mom always takes my side.
팔은 안으로 굽는다.e: An arm only bends inward, toward your own body, never outward: people naturally side with those close to them.
팔은 안으로 굽는다.t: Pronounced [파른 아느로 굼는다]. Used to point out or excuse bias toward family, friends or one's own team. This 굽다 'to bend' is regular (굽어요), unlike 굽다 'to grill' (구워요).
rel: birds of a feather stick together
nb: 가는 말이 고와야 오는 말이 곱다

혈중.ex: 운전자의 혈중 알코올 농도가 기준을 넘었습니다.
혈중.x: The driver's blood alcohol level exceeded the limit.
혈중.e: Literally 'in the blood'; almost always before another noun.
혈중.t: Used like a prefix: 혈중 농도 (blood level), 혈중 콜레스테롤, 혈중 알코올 농도.

구비문학.ex: 민요, 설화, 판소리는 모두 구비문학에 속해요.
구비문학.x: Folk songs, tales and pansori all belong to oral literature.
구비문학.e: Literally 'mouth-monument literature' — kept in memory and passed on by word of mouth.

주동인물.ex: 주동인물은 이야기를 이끌어 가는 중심 인물이에요.
주동인물.x: The protagonist is the central character who drives the story.
주동인물.e: Literally 'main-moving person' — the character who drives the action.
주동인물.t: 주인공 is the everyday word; 주동인물 is the class term, always paired with 반동인물.

교양소설.ex: 괴테의 빌헬름 마이스터는 대표적인 교양소설로 꼽혀요.
교양소설.x: Goethe's Wilhelm Meister is considered a classic Bildungsroman.
교양소설.e: A translation of German 'Bildungsroman' — literally 'cultivation novel'.
교양소설.t: Close to 성장소설, but stresses the hero's intellectual and moral growth; used mostly for European novels.

주석.ex: 어려운 단어에는 페이지 아래에 주석이 달려 있어요.
주석.x: Difficult words have notes at the bottom of the page.
주석.e: Literally 'note and interpret'; homonyms mean 'tin' and 'chairman'.
주석.t: Collocation: 주석을 달다 'to add notes'; programmers also use 주석 for a code comment.

발탁하다.m: to select, to pick out (for a position)
발탁하다.x: The director picked an unknown actor for the lead role.
발탁하다.e: Literally 'pull out and pick': choosing a talent from many.

유유자적.m: living a carefree, leisurely life at one's own pace
유유자적.ex: 은퇴 후 그는 바닷가에서 유유자적하며 살고 있어요.
유유자적.x: Since retiring, he has been living a leisurely life by the sea.
유유자적.e: Literally 'easygoing and doing what suits oneself.'
유유자적.t: Works as a verb with 하다: 유유자적하다 'to live a carefree life.'

호구지책.m: a way to make a bare living, means of subsistence
호구지책.ex: 젊은 시절 그는 호구지책으로 공사장에서 막노동을 했어요.
호구지책.x: When he was young, he did construction labor just to make ends meet.
호구지책.e: Literally 'a plan to paste the mouth' — just enough to keep from starving.
호구지책.t: Don't confuse it with 호구 'pushover' — a different, unrelated slang word.

제척기간.m: exclusion period, statutory time limit for a right
제척기간.ex: 이 권리는 제척기간이 지나면 행사할 수 없습니다.
제척기간.x: This right cannot be exercised once the exclusion period has passed.
제척기간.e: Literally 'period after which a right is cut off'.
제척기간.t: Pronounced [제척끼간]; differs from 소멸시효 because it can't be interrupted or extended.
